audit.whatIsWrong: Mortal Will is described as a damage-blocking passive in six fields: whys[1] ('absorbs your auto follow-up'), spikes[1].text ('blocks one auto or turret shot every few autos'), content.early (twice, including 'he cannot block your skillshots with Mortal Will, only auto attacks'), content.late ('passive block') and wants.foe[1] ('Spend Mortal Will passive stacks to block your auto-attack follow-ups'). Mortal Will blocks nothing.
audit.why: Riot's text is one sentence: 'Every few spells or attacks, Pantheon's next spell is empowered.' It is a damage-amplifier counter, not a block. The old block passive was removed. This is worse than a naming slip because the page builds real instructions on it — content.early tells the reader to watch for the passive to proc on a minion and throw W into that window, which is advice for a mechanic that does not exist, and it teaches the player to expect their autos to be eaten when they will not be.
audit.corrected: All six rewritten around what Mortal Will actually does: count his casts, and the empowered Comet Spear is the spike to avoid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Aegis Assault is absent from the entire page — it appears in no field in either layer, despite being the ability that decides whether Swain's commit is wasted.
audit.why: Aegis Assault makes Pantheon invulnerable to damage from the FRONT while he strikes, and it carries both the untargetable and the channel flags — a channel is interruptible, so Nevermove's root cancels it outright. It is 22/21/20/19/18s, the longest cooldown in his basic kit. Two pieces of play follow and neither was on the page: do not dump burst into the front of it, and if your root is up you do not have to wait it out at all.
audit.corrected: tldr, dosFull[2].d, dontsFull[1] (title and description) and wants.you[0] now cover it.
sources: enemyKit E text, flags (untargetable, channel, shield), cd

audit.whatIsWrong: Chart rows 0, 3, 4 and 6 disagreed with the packet in both layers. The mirror recorded 'Left as found' for this point, so it was never reconciled from either side.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is Pantheon x6 then Swain, and this page's prose says exactly that in plain words: content.early 'Pantheon owns you completely at levels 1 through 3', content.mid 'Levels 4 through 6 are still Pantheon's lane', content.late 'Past two items Swain completely outpaces Pantheon'. whys[0], whys[3], whys[4] and whys[6] agree. Rows 1, 2 and 5 already read Pantheon.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 3, 4 flipped to Pantheon and row 6 to Swain in both layers as one atomic group, ratings rescaled.

audit.whatIsWrong: No real cooldowns anywhere, and Shield Vault is described only as 'His all-in start' and 'point-and-click'.
audit.why: Shield Vault is a 600-range targeted dash that stuns AND resets his auto-attack, on 13/12/11/10/9s. The auto reset is the burst tell the missing-interactions file calls out, and it is why the damage arrives a beat sooner than the stun animation suggests. Comet Spear is 575 range on 11-8s. Grand Starfall is 180/165/150s — a very long cooldown the page tells you to punish without ever saying how long you have.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d, report[5].t and content.early now carry the numbers and the reset.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two smaller slot errors. content.late says 'your W root enables E' — Swain's W is Vision of Empire and does not root. content.early says your root arrives late 'because you are already knocked up' — Shield Vault stuns, it does not knock up.
audit.why: The mirror flagged the identical W-root crossover from Pantheon's side ('Land E pull into W root' — Vision of Empire slows and reveals at 5500-7500, Nevermove is the root). Stun versus knockup matters because tenacity and cleanse behave differently on each.
audit.corrected: Both fixed in the late and early rewrites.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[1] was titled 'Sit low for his W execute'. Shield Vault has no execute component.
audit.why: Riot's W text is 'Pantheon dashes to a target, damaging and stunning them' — no threshold damage. Nothing else in the kit carries an execute flag either.
audit.corrected: Retitled to the real mistake: dumping burst into the front of Aegis Assault.

edits.before: Pantheon owns you completely at levels 1 through 3. His W (Shield Vault) is point-and-click — he walks up, stuns you, lands the empowered Q spear, and your E root arrives too late to matter because you are already knocked up. Do not fish for E aggressively before level 3; his passive (Mortal Will) blocks the auto follow-up even when you do land the root, and his burst at levels 1-2 will straight-up kill you if you are not at full health. Play at the absolute tip of W range, poke passively, and accept that you are farming under pressure. Every time you see his passive proc on a minion, that is the window to throw a W — he cannot block your skillshots with Mortal Will, only auto attacks.
edits.after: Pantheon owns you completely at levels 1 through 3. Shield Vault is a targeted dash on 13s that stuns and resets his auto, so he closes, stuns, and lands an empowered Comet Spear before your root can arrive. Do not fish for E aggressively before level 3; Mortal Will empowers his next spell every few casts, so the spear that follows the stun is the one that kills you if you are not at full health. Play at the absolute tip of W range, poke passively, and accept that you are farming under pressure. Count his casts on the wave — the trade worth taking is the one right after an empowered spell is spent, not the one before it.

edits.before: Past two items Swain completely outpaces Pantheon. His early-game kit — Shield Vault stun, empowered spear, passive block — does not scale with items the way your Liandry's-Shadowflame-R healing snowball does. In extended 1v1s your W root enables E reliably once he has burned Shield Vault, and Demonic Ascension heals through his entire damage output. Force long side-lane fights and skirmishes over objectives where your drain wins the attrition. The one danger late: Pantheon's R can regroup his team in teamfights for a burst combo — stay outside the landing zone and force him to walk in without the surprise.
edits.after: Past two items Swain completely outpaces Pantheon. His early-game kit — Shield Vault stun, empowered spear, Aegis Assault — does not scale with items the way your Liandry's-Shadowflame-R healing snowball does. In extended 1v1s Vision of Empire's slow sets up Nevermove reliably once he has burned Shield Vault, and Demonic Ascension heals through his entire damage output. Force long side-lane fights and skirmishes over objectives where your drain wins the attrition. The one danger late: Grand Starfall can drop him into a teamfight for a burst combo — stay outside the landing zone and force him to walk in without the surprise.

notes: Medium confidence on one point worth naming. Nevermove cancelling Aegis Assault follows from the kit file's own 'channel — interruptible, any CC cancels it' flag, and I have written it into four fields. Riot's E description does not itself use the word channel, so this rests on the derived flag rather than on Riot's text. It is the single most useful thing on the page if it is right and it is a confident claim on a page if it is wrong — worth one practice-tool check before this ships. The rest of the page's Aegis Assault advice (do not burst the front, it is 22s at rank 1) holds regardless.
